form_analysis.feedback: Excellent targeted aftercare for a specialised peel. Clearly explains the unique benefits for oily, acne-prone, AND pigmented/darker skin tones. Provides appropriate cautions while reinforcing its safety profile. Good for managing expectations of minimal irritation.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare advice is for a mandelic acid peel. Mandelic acid is an alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA) with a larger molecular size, allowing for slow, even penetration. It is antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and ideal for acne-prone, oily, and darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick III-VI) due to a lower risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH).

instructions.general_directive: Please follow the General Chemical Peel Principles. The notes below are specific to mandelic acid peels.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Treatment Symptoms and Timeline
sections.content: You may feel a very mild tingling. Significant stinging is uncommon. Skin may be slightly pink for 1-12 hours. Visible peeling is often minimal to nonexistent; you may experience only light flaking 2-3 days post-treatment. Your skin may feel smoother immediately.

sections.title: Specific Instructions for Key Concerns
items: Acne and Oil Control: Mandelic acid is lipid-soluble, effectively penetrating oily pores. A mild purge is possible. Use oil-free, non-comedogenic moisturizers.

Hyperpigmentation and Darker Skin Tones: Its gentle nature makes it a preferred choice for treating melasma and PIH. However, SUN PROTECTION IS STILL ABSOLUTELY CRITICAL. Use SPF 30+ daily to prevent dark spots from worsening.
Sensitive Skin: Well-tolerated. You may experience less redness and irritation compared to other AHAs.
Product Restart: You may resume other acne or brightening products after 3-5 days, unless otherwise instructed.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions
sections.content: Avoid strenuous exercise and heat for 24-48 hours as a general precaution.

sections.title: Makeup
sections.content: You can typically apply makeup within a few hours.

sections.title: General Side Effects and Results Assessment
items: Adverse reactions are rare. Contact your practitioner if you experience unusual redness, itching, or swelling.
Results include reduced acne lesions, less oiliness, improved texture, and a more even skin tone. Improvement in pigmentation requires a series of treatments.
A series of 4-6 peels (every 1-2 weeks for acne, 2-4 weeks for pigmentation) is typical.
This peel is an excellent 'starter' peel for almost all skin types and concerns.
